section: Conservation - in-situ (protected areas, biosphere reserves) and ex-situ (zoos, gene banks, seed banks)
subsections: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30

accepted.s: In 2014, what proportion of the world's land area and coastal-marine area was covered by protected areas, respectively?
accepted.x: In 2014, protected areas covered 15.2% of global land and 8.4% of coastal and marine areas.
accepted.tq: Use the paired figures carefully and avoid reversing the land and marine percentages.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present trend in global ocean protection?
o: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected.
Nearly 30% of the ocean is protected, including 15% that is fully protected.
Only 1.66% of the ocean is protected, while nearly 10% is fully protected.
The proportion of protected ocean area has declined since 2014.
accepted.x: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected; merely 1.66% of the high seas is protected.
accepted.tq: Split the overall figure from the stricter category of fully or highly protected areas.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: By what approximate factor must marine protection increase by 2030 according to the stated assessment?
o: It must increase fivefold.
It need not increase if land protection expands.
It must triple.
It must double.
accepted.x: Marine protection must triple by 2030 to support the stated conservation goal.
accepted.tq: Identify the action word attached to the target rather than confusing it with the existing percentage.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 30x30 target was adopted under which framework and event?
o: Paris Agreement at UNFCCC COP-21 in 2015
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework at CBD COP-15 in 2022
Ramsar Convention at COP-14 in 2022
Montreal Protocol at UNEP COP-10 in 2010
accepted.x: The target forms part of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework adopted at CBD COP-15 in 2022.
accepted.tq: Match the target with its correct convention framework and conference.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation maintains the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) in collaboration with IUCN?
o: UNEP-WCMC
FAO
UNDP
UNFCCC Secretariat
accepted.x: The WDPA is run by UNEP-WCMC, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-identity trap by distinguishing UNEP-WCMC from neighbouring UN bodies.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's protected-area network:
1. Only 5.32% of India's area is inside the protected-area network.
2. The network comprised 1,134 protected areas as of 2026.
3. The number of protected areas had declined from 981 in 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the number increased from 981 in 2020 to 1,134 in 2026.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed trend in statement 3; the numerical increase is the key discriminator.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The total area covered by India's National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, respectively, was reported as:
o: 44,374 sq km and 75,796 sq km
1,22,420 sq km and 44,374 sq km
84,488 sq km and 75,796 sq km
44,374 sq km and 1,22,420 sq km
accepted.x: The National Parks covered 44,374 sq km, while Wildlife Sanctuaries covered 1,22,420 sq km.
accepted.tq: Keep the category-area pairing intact; the main trap is reversal of the two figures.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about a National Park is correct?
o: It permits all human activities after consultation with local communities.
It is an area outside the formal protected-area network.
It is declared only on private land when a community volunteers.
It is governed under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and provides the highest protection, with no rights allowed.
accepted.x: National Parks are governed by the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and provide the highest level of protection, with no rights allowed within them.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal basis and the distinguishing degree of protection.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the principal distinction between a Wildlife Sanctuary and a National Park?
o: Human activity may be regulated and permitted to an extent in a Wildlife Sanctuary, whereas a National Park provides the highest protection.
A National Park is outside the protected-area network, whereas a Wildlife Sanctuary is inside it.
Only Wildlife Sanctuaries can be declared under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
A Wildlife Sanctuary has no legal basis, whereas a National Park has one.
accepted.x: Both are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, but human activity is regulated and permitted to an extent in a Wildlife Sanctuary; National Parks have higher protection.
accepted.tq: Compare the degree of permissible human activity instead of confusing the common legal basis.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Conservation Reserve is generally declared by the State Government:
o: Only on land acquired by the Union Government
On private or community land when a community volunteers
On government land, usually adjoining or linking protected areas, after consulting local people
Only outside the formal protected-area network under the CBD
accepted.x: A Conservation Reserve is declared on government land, usually adjoining or linking protected areas, after consultation with local communities. It derives from the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife Protection Act.
accepted.tq: Ask who declares it, on what land, and after whose consultation.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Community Reserve differs from a Conservation Reserve because it is generally declared:
o: Only in marine areas under the CBD
On government land adjoining a National Park
On private or community land when the community volunteers
Only by the Union Government without local consultation
accepted.x: A Community Reserve is declared by the State on private or community land when the community volunteers. Both categories were provided for through the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife Protection Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the two reserve types by land ownership and the role of community consent.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM) is best described as:
o: A temporary area protected only during a breeding season
An ex-situ facility for storing genetic material
An area outside the formal protected-area network that delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes
A formally notified National Park with the highest legal protection
accepted.x: An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.
accepted.tq: Use the outside-the-network distinction to separate OECMs from formal protected areas.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an OECM?
o: Recognition automatically changes land ownership and confers new legal authority.
It delivers lasting conservation benefits.
It is demarcated and has inclusive governance.
It is outside the formal protected-area network.
accepted.x: Recognition of an OECM is outcome-based and does not change land ownership or confer new legal, financial or management authority. The other three are among its criteria.
accepted.tq: Look for the statement that reverses the no-new-authority feature of an OECM.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following sets contains the four criteria associated with recognition of an OECM?
1. Being outside the formal protected-area network
2. Being demarcated
3. Having inclusive governance
4. Providing lasting benefits
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The four stated criteria are being outside the formal protected-area network, being demarcated, having inclusive governance and providing lasting benefits.
accepted.tq: When all listed criteria are distinct and compatible, test the complete combination rather than a partial code.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's first OECM, recognised in 2022, is:
o: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, Tamil Nadu
Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Meghalaya
Great Himalayan National Park, Himachal Pradesh
accepted.x: Aravalli Biodiversity Park in Gurugram, a restored mining site, was recognised as India's first OECM in 2022.
accepted.tq: Combine the identity, location and year to avoid confusing an OECM with a biosphere reserve or National Park.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proposed OECMs in Andhra Pradesh are intended to include areas such as:
o: Only privately owned agricultural fields
Only National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
Sacred groves, wetlands and industrial greenbelts outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
Only marine areas beyond the territorial sea
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board plans OECMs outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, wetlands and industrial greenbelts.
accepted.tq: Apply the outside-formal-reserves requirement to the examples of proposed sites.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India had 58 Tiger Reserves as of 2026.
2. The number of Tiger Reserves increased from 9 in 1973 to 58.
3. Tiger Reserves constituted approximately 30% of India's land area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The area of Tiger Reserves was approximately 2.6% of India's land, not 30%, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Reject the exaggerated percentage while retaining the correct count and historical comparison.
accepted.sec: Protected area coverage - global data, OECMs, 30x30  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly classifies all the listed sites as in-situ conservation methods?
o: Zoo, botanical garden, seed bank and gene bank
National Park, sacred grove, biosphere reserve and OECM
Cryopreservation, tissue culture, zoo and captive breeding
Pollen bank, field gene bank, seed bank and botanical garden
accepted.x: National Parks, sacred groves, biosphere reserves and OECMs conserve species in their natural or associated habitat and are in-situ methods.
accepted.tq: Use the on-site versus off-site test and identify the group containing only habitat-based measures.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an EX-SITU conservation method?
o: Tiger reserve
Sacred lake
Community reserve
Field gene bank
accepted.x: A field gene bank is an ex-situ method because genetic resources are maintained away from their original natural habitat. Sacred lakes, community reserves and Tiger Reserves are in-situ measures.
accepted.tq: Find the off-site storage method among habitat-based conservation areas.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: In-situ — cryopreservation of embryos
Ex-situ — National Park
In-situ — conservation reserve
Ex-situ — sacred grove
accepted.x: A Conservation Reserve is an in-situ method because conservation occurs on site. Cryopreservation is ex-situ, while National Parks and sacred groves are in-situ.
accepted.tq: Check whether the method preserves organisms on site or away from their natural habitat.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: In-situ conservation is generally considered the most effective method because it:
o: Eliminates the need for protected areas
Can conserve only genetic material and not living species
Keeps species interacting with their environment
Stores all organisms in artificial conditions
accepted.x: In-situ conservation maintains species within their natural environment, allowing continued ecological interactions and processes.
accepted.tq: Link the method to its ecological advantage rather than to storage or artificial propagation.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are examples of ex-situ conservation?
1. Seed and gene banks
2. Cryopreservation of gametes and embryos
3. Botanical gardens and zoos
4. Tissue culture banks
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four are ex-situ methods because they conserve plants, animals or genetic material away from the original natural habitat.
accepted.tq: Test the complete list by applying the single off-site principle to each item.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Meristem culture is particularly useful in ex-situ conservation because it enables:
o: Conversion of a Community Reserve into a National Park
Virus-free propagation of plants
Protection of animals in a wildlife sanctuary
Natural pollination in a protected forest
accepted.x: Meristem culture is a tissue-culture technique used for virus-free propagation of plants.
accepted.tq: Associate the specialised biotechnology term with its direct application rather than with a protected-area category.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an appropriate example of captive breeding as an ex-situ conservation intervention?
o: Protecting a wetland as an OECM
Declaring a sacred grove as a Community Reserve
Breeding Gangetic gharials and releasing them into suitable rivers
Regulating tourism in a National Park
accepted.x: Captive breeding is suitable when a species' habitat has been permanently lost; bred animals may subsequently be released, as in the reintroduction of Gangetic gharials in several states.
accepted.tq: Recognise the sequence of off-site breeding followed by release into the wild.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation of ex-situ conservation?
o: Maintaining captive populations can be resource-intensive.
It may support education, research and reintroduction.
It cannot by itself save the entire ecosystem.
It requires considerable space and money.
accepted.x: Education, research and reintroduction are values of ex-situ conservation, not limitations. Space and financial requirements, as well as inability to save the whole ecosystem, are limitations.
accepted.tq: Separate benefits from limitations before selecting the exception.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Ex-situ conservation cannot by itself conserve the entire ecosystem.
Reason (R): Ex-situ conservation maintains selected species or genetic material away from their natural habitat.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. Since ex-situ conservation removes selected organisms or genetic material from the natural ecological setting, it cannot preserve all ecosystem interactions and processes.
accepted.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains why off-site conservation cannot preserve the whole ecosystem.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sacred grove — in-situ conservation
Cryopreservation of gametes — in-situ conservation
Pollen bank — ex-situ conservation
Animal translocation — ex-situ intervention
accepted.x: Cryopreservation of gametes is an ex-situ method because gametes are preserved away from the natural habitat. Pollen banks, sacred groves and translocation are correctly matched as stated.
accepted.tq: Use the off-site storage clue to detect the reversed classification.
accepted.sec: In-situ vs ex-situ - classify methods  [other exams]
